summary: As of Wednesday, September 30, before the U.S. open, the Nasdaq setup is fragile rather than outright bearish. Tuesday's Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.08% as the 10-year Treasury yield briefly reached about 5.29%, its highest since 2007, before easing; the S&P 500 and Dow also finished modestly lower. Softer JOLTS job openings and a sharp drop in consumer confidence helped pull yields off their highs, while New York Fed President John Williams said there was no need for urgency on another rate increase. That leaves technology caught between still-resilient AI leadership and a discount-rate backdrop that remains unusually restrictive.

The biggest issue today is event concentration. August PCE inflation and the third estimate of Q2 GDP arrive together at 8:30 ET, immediately after ADP private payrolls at 8:15 ET, creating a direct test of whether Tuesday's modest rate relief can continue. Oil and Middle East headlines remain an important counterweight: by the cutoff, the U.S. had announced another offer to loan up to 40 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, while Washington also imposed fresh Iran-related sanctions. Micron reports after the close, making memory/AI demand and guidance a major semiconductor read-through. A reliable Nasdaq futures quote for the requested 06:00 Turkey-time cutoff was not available, so no later overnight futures move is used here.

events.title: 1. ADP private payrolls — 8:15 ET
events.detail: September ADP employment is the first major U.S. labor signal of the morning. With yields already near multi-decade highs, a materially stronger labor reading could revive rate-hike pressure; a softer print would reinforce Tuesday's signs of cooling labor demand.

events.title: 2. PCE inflation, personal income/spending and final Q2 GDP — 8:30 ET
events.detail: This is the day's dominant pre-market catalyst. PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, while income/spending show demand strength and the GDP revision adds growth context. A hotter inflation/strong-demand combination would be the clearest threat to Nasdaq through higher Treasury yields; cooler inflation would give long-duration technology the best chance of relief.

events.title: 3. EIA petroleum inventories — 10:30 ET
events.detail: Oil remains unusually important because the Middle East conflict has transmitted directly into inflation expectations and Treasury yields. The EIA report can amplify or offset the geopolitical oil premium during the cash session.

events.title: 4. Micron fiscal Q4 earnings — after the close; call 4:30 ET
events.detail: Micron is a major AI-memory and semiconductor-cycle catalyst. Beyond the headline numbers, demand, pricing, capacity and forward guidance can influence the broader semiconductor complex and the market's confidence in AI infrastructure spending.

events.title: 5. U.S.–Iran/Hormuz headlines — unscheduled
events.detail: Geopolitical risk remains capable of overriding the calendar through crude oil. The U.S. announced fresh Iran-related sanctions Tuesday even as efforts to stabilize energy supply continued, so any escalation or credible de-escalation can quickly feed into oil, inflation expectations, yields and Nasdaq valuation.

watchIntoOpen: What I’d watch into the open: the clean upside scenario is softer or in-line PCE, no upside growth surprise, and a 10-year yield that retreats from Tuesday's extreme levels while semiconductor leadership holds. The downside scenario is a hot inflation/strong-demand combination that pushes the 10-year back toward or through Tuesday's high, especially if oil strengthens at the same time. Because Micron reports after the bell, intraday semiconductor positioning may also become more cautious even if the macro data are benign. The strongest confirmation of a constructive Nasdaq session would therefore be falling yields plus broad chip participation; a mega-cap-only rebound with yields still above 5% would be less convincing.
